text:
Maya: CI alert — nightly harness flagged a regression for candidate-kernel v3 on A100 longseq (seqlen=4096) with batching enabled. p99 up ~12%, p95 up ~6%. ci-bot attached artifacts. Anyone able to pick this up? :eyes:

ci-bot: Perf job run-2026-03-17-03:12:34 finished. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/nightly/1755551234/v3/ . Summary: p50 +0.8ms, p95 +6.1%, p99 +12.4% (A100, batch=8). Ampere-midseq unaffected. Note: microprobe reports KV_CACHE hit ratio drop from 0.78 -> 0.52 for longseq cases.

Tony: I pulled the flame and microprobe logs. Repro command I used locally: ```./tools/bench_micro --kernel candidate_v3 --device A100 --seqlen 4096 --batch 8 --profile microprobe``` Output snippet: 
```
KV_CACHE: hits=5120 misses=4700 hit_ratio=0.52
p99: 23.8ms (baseline 21.2ms)
backend: longseq-path used: true
```
Feels like the kernel's prefetch pattern increased eviction churn when batch>4.

Leah: Hypothesis: v3 changed loop tile size and introduced a slightly different memory footprint for KV buffers; with our continuous batching the per-request KV windows overlap more and cause extra misses. Quick checks: rerun with KV_CACHE=off and with batch=4/2 to see p99 delta.

Arnav: Also check the autotuner pick logs — if the path selector now prefers the longseq kernel for sequences just above threshold, that could increase KV pressure. Dump the pick decisions: `./tools/pick_dump --job run-1755551234 --filter candidate_v3` That will show sequence buckets and chosen kernel variant.

Zach: Two mitigations: 1) Add a gating step in perf CI requiring KV hit ratio within +/-5% of baseline for candidate promotion. 2) If confirmed, revert the tile change in v3 or add a variant with conservative prefetch for high-batch/longseq.

Tony: Re-ran local microbench with KV_CACHE disabled: ```./tools/bench_micro --kernel candidate_v3 --device A100 --seqlen 4096 --batch 8 --kv_cache disabled``` Results: p99 21.5ms (baselined), hit_ratio N/A. So it's KV-related. Also ran batch=4 with KV enabled: hit_ratio 0.74 p99 21.7ms.

Maya: Good repro. Can we triage root cause (prefetch tiling vs allocator fragmentation) before next nightly? If not, let's disable candidate_v3 from autopick until fix.

Tony: I'll take triage. Opening issue and temporary disable. Issue: https://git.internal/redwood/issues/INF-4821 — labels: perf-regression, triage, blocker. I'll also add a failing microprobe test to catch this.

ci-bot: Shelving candidate_v3 from nightly autopick: action=disable candidate=candidate_v3 scope=nightly. Reason=KV hit ratio regression on A100 longseq.

Leah: Suggested debug steps for Tony: 1) instrument per-batch kv footprint, 2) run allocation-free replay to check fragmentation, 3) test a v3 variant that reduces prefetch depth by 25%.

Tony: Plan: run steps 1-3 today, post detailed microprobe traces and a diff of the kernel tile sizes. If quick fix found, I'll re-enable with gated rollout behind KV-hit check.

Zach: Sounds good. Also adding CI requirement: PRs modifying kernel tiling must include microbench matrix (A100, batch 2/4/8, seqlen 512/2048/4096) and KV hit ratio report.

Maya: Thanks all — assigning follow-ups: Tony (triage + issue), Leah (kv instrumentation helpers), Arnav (pick-dump + autotuner logs), Zach (CI gating PR). :thumbsup:

Tony: I'll post an initial triage note by EOD and link artifacts here.

ci-bot: Noted. Tagging nightly owners. :robot_face:

Maya: Closing loop — once Tony confirms a fix or provides a rollback PR, we'll bump candidate back into the harness with the new KV checks.

(threads like this are intentionally short; will drop updates into the issue and attach perf dumps.)
